summary: This bill temporarily raises base pay by 35% for federal correctional officers and certain Bureau of Prisons wage-system employees, with the increase set to expire after five years unless a DOJ Inspector General review finds measurable reductions in staff augmentation and mandatory overtime.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates new special base rates of pay for federal correctional officers by increasing applicable General Schedule or LEO rates by 35 percent (with caps), and it directs a similar 35 percent wage increase for certain prevailing-rate Bureau of Prisons employees. These changes directly raise federal compensation expenditures for an entire occupational category. The effect is therefore an expansion of government spending rather than a reduction.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms.
No provisions address health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, public option, or market-based health-care delivery.
No provisions regulate firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment rights.
No provisions alter immigration pathways, border enforcement, visas, or protections for non-citizens.
No provisions address reproductive health services, funding restrictions, or access to abortion.
The pay adjustments apply exclusively to Bureau of Prisons employees under the Department of Justice; they do not affect Department of Defense or military compensation.
No provisions modify environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation programs.
No provisions expand or contract means-tested benefit programs such as SNAP, TANF, or housing assistance.
No provisions address school funding, federal education programs, school choice, or privatization.
No provisions alter drug scheduling, enforcement priorities, or decriminalization measures.

While the bill concerns federal correctional officers, it addresses only their compensation levels and contains no language on sentencing policy, policing practices, rehabilitation programs, or mandatory minimums.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.

The bill increases mandatory federal outlays but does not contain any debt-ceiling, deficit-reduction target, or PAYGO provisions; the spending impact is therefore incidental rather than a deliberate stance on debt reduction.
No provisions expand or restrict legal protections or benefits on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
No provisions appropriate or modify funding for foreign assistance programs.
No provisions address voter access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions regulate data privacy, surveillance, or technology company oversight.
The bill mandates higher base pay for a class of federal employees but does not alter collective-bargaining rights, union representation procedures, or employer flexibility in labor relations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or anti-discrimination requirements.
